stem:
A 59-year-old man with a brainstem stroke loses his normal automatic breathing rhythm and must consciously initiate each breath.

A lesion in which of the following structures most directly explains the loss of his involuntary breathing rhythm?

options.label: A
options.text: Primary motor cortex projections to the diaphragm
options.misconception: The voluntary pathway is being blamed for loss of the automatic one.
options.explanation: He can still breathe consciously, so voluntary cortical control is intact; the lost function is the medullary rhythm generator.

options.label: B
options.text: Dorsal respiratory group in the medulla oblongata
options.misconception: None; the DRG maintains the constant breathing rhythm.
options.explanation: The dorsal respiratory group is involved in maintaining a constant breathing rhythm by stimulating the diaphragm and intercostal muscles to contract; destroying it abolishes automatic inspiration.

options.label: C
options.text: Ventral respiratory group in the medulla oblongata
options.misconception: The forced-breathing group is being confused with the quiet-rhythm group.
options.explanation: The ventral respiratory group is involved in forced breathing, stimulating accessory muscles; baseline quiet rhythm depends on the dorsal group.

options.label: D
options.misconception: A pontine modulatory center is being assigned the rhythm-generating role.
options.explanation: Pontine centers influence and modify the medullary pattern; the constant rhythm itself is generated by the medullary dorsal respiratory group.

options.label: E
options.misconception: An inhibitory rate-control center is being confused with the rhythm source.
options.explanation: The pneumotaxic center inhibits dorsal respiratory group activity to control the rate of breathing; it does not generate the rhythm that was lost.

context: Learning objective: localize the breathing rhythm generator. The medulla oblongata contains the dorsal respiratory group (constant rhythm, drives diaphragm and intercostals) and the ventral respiratory group (forced breathing).
imageCaption: V/Q, PO2 gradient, CO2 transport + chloride shift, chemoreceptors, brainstem, Dalton/Henry.
